questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The scientific study of the structure and form of animals and plants
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 (Morphology)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Morphology"** refers to the scientific study of the structure, form, and organization of animals and plants. (संरचना विज्ञान)

 
 
• **Example:** The morphology of flowers often helps botanists classify different plant species.
 
 
 
• **"Structure and form of animals and plants"** is the definition of Morphology, making it the most appropriate one-word substitute. (संरचना और रूप विज्ञान)
 
 
• **Example:** Researchers used morphology to analyze the skeletal differences between the two species.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 (Morphology)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Zoology** (प्राणी विज्ञान): The scientific study of animals, their biology, behavior, and classification.

 
 
• **Example:** She decided to major in zoology to study the behavior of wild animals.
 
 
 
• **Biology** (जीव विज्ञान): The scientific study of life and living organisms.
 
 
• **Example:** Biology covers a wide range of topics, including genetics, ecology, and anatomy.
 
 
 
• **Botany** (वनस्पति विज्ञान): The scientific study of plants, including their physiology, structure, and classification.
 
 
• **Example:** Botany helps us understand the importance of plants in maintaining the ecosystem.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Like a dying duck in a thunderstorm
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 (Dejected or hopeless)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Like a dying duck in a thunderstorm"** refers to someone who is extremely dejected, hopeless, or in a pitiable state. (अत्यंत निराश या असहाय स्थिति में)

 
 
• **Example:** After losing the championship match, he looked like a dying duck in a thunderstorm, unable to hide his disappointment.
 
 
 
• **"Dejected or hopeless"** means feeling downhearted or in despair, often when faced with failure or adversity. (हताश या निराश)
 
 
• **Example:** After failing the exam, she felt completely dejected and hopeless, unsure of what to do next.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom **"Like a dying duck in a thunderstorm"** correctly conveys the meaning of being dejected or hopeless.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 (Dejected or hopeless)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Fearful or scared of water** (पानी से डरना): This option is incorrect as the idiom does not relate to fear of water.

 
 
• **Example:** Many people are fearful of water due to past traumatic experiences.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Bad swimmer or practitioner** (खराब तैराक या अभ्यासकर्ता): This option is incorrect as the idiom does not imply poor swimming or skill.
 
 
• **Example:** He is a bad swimmer and avoids going to the pool.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Harmful or vigilant** (हानिकारक या चौकस): This option is incorrect as the idiom does not denote harm or alertness.
 
 
• **Example:** The teacher is always vigilant during exams to prevent cheating.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.

options.text: A lot of books and notes place in order look most fascinating.
A lot of books and notes placed in order look fascinating.
A lot of books and notes placed on order looks most fascinating.
A lot of book and notes placed in order looks most fascinating.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. A lot of books and notes placed in order look fascinating .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence must be grammatically correct and in proper agreement with the subject.
 
• In option 2, the subject "A lot of books and notes" is plural, and the verb "look" correctly agrees with the plural subject.
 
• Option 1 is incorrect because "place" is used instead of "placed," making the sentence grammatically incorrect.
 
• Option 3 is incorrect because "on order" is used instead of "in order," and "looks" does not agree with the plural subject.
 
• Option 4 is incorrect because "book" should be plural ("books") to agree with "notes," and "looks" does not agree with the plural subject.

Correct sentence: *A lot of books and notes placed in order look fascinating*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When the subject is plural, the verb must agree with it. For example:
 
 
• **Correct:** The books and notes look interesting.
 
• **Incorrect:** The books and notes looks interesting.
 
 
 
• Proper placement of phrases like "in order" is crucial for clarity and correctness.
 
• Always check the verb tense and subject-verb agreement to ensure grammatical accuracy.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The train is running / late by six hours / so it / cannot make over the time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. cannot make over the time .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"make over the time"** is incorrect because the proper expression is **"make up the time"**, which means to compensate for lost time.
 
• The sentence describes a delay in the train’s schedule, and it is not possible to recover the time lost due to the delay.
 
• Thus, the error lies in segment 2: **"cannot make over the time".**

Correct sentence: *The train is running late by six hours, so it **cannot make up the time**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common phrases with "make":**

 
 
• **Make up for:** To compensate for something.
 
**Example:** He worked hard to make up for the lost time.
 
• **Make up:** To reconcile or resolve a conflict.
 
**Example:** They finally made up after their argument.
 
 
 
• **Usage of "make up the time":**
 
 
• It is commonly used in contexts like travel or schedules to indicate recovering lost time.
